transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I go out of my way to avoid anything that reminds me of what happened to my cousin, even if it means cutting out parts of my life. Ever since he was killed in Guatemala, I've been avoiding public transit, the news, and even my own community just to cope. It has gotten to the point where I feel like I'm barely living my normal life anymore.

Do memories of your cousin’s killing come back in unwanted, distressing ways—like nightmares, flashbacks, or feeling as if it’s happening again? Also, were you there to witness it or directly exposed to the details of what happened?

I wasn't there when the shooting happened, but I arrived in Guatemala afterward, viewed his body, and heard my aunt describe the attack in graphic detail. Now, I constantly get unwanted, vivid memories of him in the coffin and her voice playing like a clip in my head, making me freeze up. I also have awful nightmares about buses and my family back home that wake me up completely exhausted.

Was your cousin’s death accidental or violent, and was hearing the graphic details from your aunt part of your job or first-responder work? Also, when did these symptoms start, and have they lasted more than a month?

My cousin's death was very violent; he was shot and killed during an armed robbery on a bus. It wasn't related to my job at all, as I work as a computer systems analyst. These symptoms started right after I returned from his funeral and have been going on steadily for a little over a year now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes exposure to a violent death of a close family member through post-event confrontation with the body and graphic details, followed by persistent intrusion symptoms, trauma-related avoidance, duration over one month, and clear functional impairment. This pattern is most consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder.
